newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Umaga may gain from Lomu's misfortune.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Umaga may gain from Lomu's misfortune.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Jan 28 - Jonah Lomu's misfortune presents Wellington Hurricanes rugby wing Tana Umaga with a good opportunity to press for higher honours this year.
Umaga has a chance to begin pressing his claims for All Blacks selection night in Gisborne when the Hurricanes have their first serious run of the season against a Lower North Island selection.
Lomu is sidelined because of a with kidney disease, and his left wing jersey is favoured to be worn by Glen Osborne.
Aucklander James Kerr and Hawke's Bay's Roger Randell have been touted as contenders also, but Umaga also looks the part after a series of impressive training sessions.
Umaga played at fullback for the Hurricanes in the inaugural Super 12 series last year, but coach Frank Oliver said there was no thought of playing Umaga anywhere other than on the wing this year.
"I see they're talking about Kerr and Randell," Oliver said yesterday.
"That should be plenty of incentive to get Tana going."
Hurricanes captain Mark Allen, big lock Mark Cooksley, fullback Christian Cullen and flanker Filo Tiatia will miss tonight's practice match at Rugby Park in Gisborne.

Allen is still overcoming a back injury, Cooksley injured his back yesterday, Tiatia still has a painful shoulder injury and Cullen is being given every chance to come right from his cartilage operation.
Oliver has three teams sorted out for the three spells of 30 minutes.
"I'm looking for a bit of rhythm, control and combination," Oliver said.
